steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The ESA gives you starting points from AQA — you choose one and develop it independently during the preparatory period.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The preparatory period is YOUR time to research, experiment and develop ideas — show the same depth as your portfolio.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The 10 hours supervised time is for producing your FINAL RESPONSE — all preparation must be complete before it starts.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Your ESA preparation must address ALL four AOs — examiners mark the preparation alongside the supervised work.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring the externally set assignment component 2. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with the externally set assignment component 2. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with the externally set assignment component 2. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to the externally set assignment component 2, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments t | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
